working_definition: Tm4 is a narrow-field transmedullary columnar neuron (one per optic column) of the adult Drosophila optic lobe. It has fine and bleb-type arborizations in medulla layers M2, M3, M4 and M9, and terminates in lobula layers 1, 2, 3 and 4. It receives input in the medulla from lamina monopolar neuron L2 and centrifugal neuron C3, and outputs in lobula layer 1 to T5 neurons. It is capable of both cholinergic and GABAergic neurotransmission and belongs to the Notch ON hemilineage of medulla neuroblasts.

best_match.fbbt_definition: Transmedullary narrow field neuron that terminates in lobula layers 1, 2 and 4 with bleb-type arborizations, and with fine arborizations in layer 3. It displays fine arborizations in medulla layers M2, M3, M4 and M9, and has bleb-type arborizations in layers M2, M4, and M9 (Morante and Desplan, 2008; Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989). In the medulla, receives input from lamina monopolar neuron L2 and centrifugal neuron C3 (Takemura et al., 2013). In lobula layer 1, it outputs to T5 neurons (Shinomiya et al., 2014). It seems to be capable of both cholinergic and GABAergic neurotransmission. There is usually one of these cells per optic column (Nern et al., 2025).

justification: FBbt:00003792 'transmedullary neuron Tm4' is an exact label match to the cluster name 'Tm4'. The FBbt definition aligns precisely with established Tm4 anatomy on every diagnostic feature: narrow-field transmedullary morphology, medulla layers M2/M3/M4/M9, lobula layers 1/2/3/4 with bleb-type and fine arborization patterns, presynaptic input from L2 and C3 in the medulla, output to T5 in lobula layer 1, dual cholinergic and GABAergic neurotransmission, and one cell per optic column. The term is not obsolete. No distinguishing features of the cluster fall outside the FBbt definition. The sibling term FBbt:00110075 'transmedullary neuron Tm4a' is a narrower subtype (lobula layer 4 only, cholinergic only) and does not represent the full Tm4 type.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Immature form of the transmedullary neuron Tm4 (Konstantinides et al., 2022). It is a Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron, born from a medulla forming neuroblast during the Hth/Opa temporal window (Konstantinides et al., 2022).
